comments.rawMarkdown:
I've definitely been doing SFT with the models. But not on RTX 6000 Pro. All on H200's. That said, I have tried a lot of different approaches and so far have not found any recipes that work. For others, I have tried...
* SFT, using the Qwen Max as a teacher and also Astra as a teacher. 
* I've trained on synthetic variants of LS20 and CD82 just to try and find a working recipe
* I've trained using just "stall" points (eg. loops or lives lost), and also on "periodic" trajectories (ie. every 10th move) where at those moments, you hand the Duck game state to the teacher, and ask the teacher to take a move and then SFT on that. 
* I've tried it with different learning rates.
* I tried with Qwen Flash - Next and with Qwen 3.8 27B.

No permutation of these has been able to make meaningful improvements. I'm pretty convinced that finetuning with Qwen Flash Next is very difficult because it's an MoE model. I think 27B is more plausible, but still haven't been able to pull it off. Would love any tips from others who've tried or had some success!

comments.rawMarkdown:
Thanks for sharing all of this, it's genuinely useful to see what didn't move the needle.

One caution on the teacher side: OpenAI's Terms of Use (effective Jan 1, 2026) list "Use Output to develop models that compete with OpenAI" as a prohibited use, so fine-tuning a model on Astra-generated moves is risky under their policy. It also gets awkward for prize eligibility, since winning solutions have to be open-sourced, and weights distilled from restricted outputs may not be cleanly releasable. Worth checking the terms of whichever teacher you use before building a training set on it.

firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
I've been toying with the idea of finetuning a model (either through SFT or some form of RL), but I haven't decided on a recipe yet. Part of the reason I've been holding off on trying this is because I'm not sure how realistic it is to fine tune Qwen 3.8 Next Flash NVFP4 on an RTX 6000 Pro.

I know that the RTX Pro is more than capable of finetuning Qwen 3.8 27B, but the gap in capability between 27B and flash next is quite large in my experiments (And I don't want to spend too much time finetuning 27B just for it to reach parity with base flash-next).

Has anyone had success training Flash-Next on their RTX 6000 Pro, or is the only option if I want to pursue finetuning to switch back to a smaller model and hope I can push it past the base performance of flash-next? Or if teams have found success training Qwen Flash Next, did you need to rent out more compute from somewhere else, and would that have an impact on the eligibility on winning the competition (if the hosts find excessive external compute not being "fair" to other participants)?

Any advice would be appreciated, and I don't expect anyone to share their "secret sauce" training recipe, especially so close to Milestone #2 and competition end.
